about: Hand-written probes for the pairs in pairs.json. For each side: two paraphrases (same meaning as the request, none of that side's cue words) and, where the side has a lexical cue at all, one keyword control (the OTHER side's request with one of this side's cue words slipped in without changing what is asked). Several customer_support pairs contrast pragmatic framing rather than vocabulary -- billing_vs_technical uses the *same* content words in a different order -- so those sides have no cue word to slip in and carry paraphrases only.

paraphrases: There is a charge on my account for something I do not seem to have.
My invoice includes a feature that is not showing up for me.
A feature I paid for is not appearing anywhere in my account.
I cannot locate the thing I purchased inside the product.
What are the steps to revoke an API key?
Where is the documented procedure for revoking an API key?
Revoking my API key is not working; please do it on my behalf.
The revoke action fails for my API key, so could someone on your side handle it?
I would like money back because rate limit headers are absent from API responses.
Please issue credit for the rate limit headers that never appeared in API responses.

keyword.request: Why are rate limit headers missing from my API responses? I do not want a refund, only an explanation.

paraphrases: What causes rate limit headers to be absent from my API responses?
Rate limit headers never show up in my API responses, and I want to understand the reason.

keyword.request: Can you refund me for missing rate limit headers in API responses? No need to explain why, just process it.

paraphrases: I just joined the team, so why can I not open this folder?
I am brand new here and this folder will not open for me.

keyword.request: I could access this folder — why can’t I now? Nothing changed except our new office network.

paraphrases: This folder used to open for me and suddenly does not.
I had access to this folder before and I have lost it.

keyword.request: New user — why can’t I access this folder? It is the one the team uses for onboarding now.

paraphrases: After switching to a cheaper plan my bill still shows the previous price.
My plan went down a tier but the amount charged did not change.
After switching to a cheaper plan the bill is unchanged, my colleagues can no longer use features, and the usage numbers have vanished.
My downgrade left three problems: the old price is still charged, teammates lost feature access, and metrics disappeared.
SSO has to be live for us by end of day; is manual approval part of our plan?
We are switching SSO on right away, so will someone have to approve it by hand?

keyword.request: Does enabling SSO require manual approval for our plan? I am asking for today’s onboarding notes, no rush.

paraphrases: For our plan, is manual approval needed to turn SSO on?
Is switching SSO on something that has to be approved by hand on our plan?
